Kim / Ben,

Summary of technical read:
- Hosted (US-EAST) is the fastest way to validate integrations and measure per-request latency. For a 512-token generation on a medium-sized model we should expect steady-state p50 ~90-120ms per-token when batching is minimal; end-to-end 512-token generation single-request p95 ~1.2-1.6s in our optimized path (depends on model variant). These are conservative targets we can commit for during the POC with a Hosted route.
- Dedicated gives predictable tail latency at scale (consistent p95 across higher concurrency). If MedDev anticipates sustained concurrent throughput during the eval (hundreds of requests/min), Dedicated will reduce variance and is easy to flip to — the main work is capacity reservation and a brief config change on the client side. We typically allocate a 3–5 business day window for a smooth switch from Hosted to Dedicated provided network/firewall rules are in place.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) is the right path for PHI or enforced KMS usage. Prep for Private includes VPC peering/VPN setup, KMS integration, audit log collection, and an on-prem approval window for our infra team. Realistically plan for 4–8 weeks depending on customer IT availability.

Risks / notes:
- If they decide mid-POC to enable customer-managed KMS, that tends to push Private timelines; we should capture the KMS decision in the MAP as a gated item.
- Recommend we formalize an SLO row in the MAP with concrete p95 placeholders and a rollback/runbook in case of performance regressions during the Dedicated trial.

I can update the MAP with a technical appendix showing expected latency bands per lane and a cutover checklist.

Hi Jordan / Elena,

Thanks for the quick responses and context. Based on Karthik's input, here's a concise recommended approach and proposed next steps (I updated the MAP to v0.2 attached):

Recommendation (fastest path to acceptance):
1) Start with Hosted in US-EAST to validate integrations and measure latency and correctness (no PHI ingest).
2) If throughput testing shows variance or they exceed concurrency targets, flip to a short Dedicated trial (3–5 business days for cutover) mid-POC.
3) If they confirm PHI or require customer-managed KMS, plan a Private engagement — we'll gate that as a separate acceptance criteria in the MAP (expected 4–8 weeks prep).

SLOs to include in MAP v0.2:
- 512-token gen: p50 per-token ~100ms, p95 end-to-end ~1.4s (hosted baseline)
- Target Dedicated window for throughput test: 3–5 business days
